dedupe_keys.name: dtumos digital twin for large scale urban mobility operating systems

description: DTUMOS is an open-source digital twin framework for urban mobility operating systems such as taxi, many-to-many pickup and depot-based delivery services. It has four parts: historical mobility data (taxi trip records, smart card data, cellular signalling or delivery records) that generate supply and demand; a machine-learning estimated time of arrival model; a vehicle routing and dispatch process on OpenStreetMap roads through the OSRM routing engine; and outputs as deck.gl trip visualisations and performance reports. It was developed by researchers of Hannam University and KAIST in Daejeon, Korea, and described in Scientific Reports (13:5154, 29 March 2023). It is location independent and runs at city scale; published implementations cover taxi services in Seoul (April 2022), New York City and Chicago and a truck delivery service on Jeju island, and a case study sized the extra taxi supply Seoul needed for late-night demand after COVID-19. The code is free on GitHub as Python notebooks for Linux (WSL2 on Windows), with online visualisations and reports. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0. DTUMOS supports digital twin, agent-based and capacity planning studies of fleet size, dispatch optimisation and policy for on-demand mobility, and complements network simulators such as MATSim and SUMO, catalogued here. The underlying files were not downloaded, so their contents are not verified here.
